content:
“Your Vault job has finally paid off!”

**Licensed Plumber** is an Intelligence-based perk in *Fallout 76*.

Pipe weapons break more slowly and are cheaper to repair (does not include the lead pipe).

| Rank | Cost | Description | Form ID | 
| ★★★ | 3 | Your pipe weapons break 60% slower and are cheaper to repair. | 0033843B | 
| ★★ | 2 | Your pipe weapons break 40% slower and are cheaper to repair. | 0033843A | 
| ★ | 1 | Your pipe weapons break 20% slower and are cheaper to repair. | 00338438 | 

- Stacks with Gunsmith and Weapon Artisan
- Licensed Plumber affects the following weapons:

| Pipe bolt-action | Pipe gun | Pipe revolver | 
| Rose's syringer | Syringer | Vox syringer | 

- Pipe weapons are 20%/40%/60% cheaper to repair.
- Prior to patch 1.0.5.10, the condition loss bonuses provided by each rank of the Licensed Plumber perk were 30%/60%/90%. Afterwards, they were reduced to 20%/40%/60% and the repair bonuses have also been reduced, to match the Power Patcher perk.
- This perk does not affect the lead pipe despite having "pipe" in its name.
- The analogous perk for armor is White Knight and Power Patcher for power armor. The closest analogous perk for non-pipe weapons is Gunsmith, though the perk has a maximum effect of 50% over five ranks rather than 60% over three ranks, as well as including access to higher-tier gun crafting recipes.

The Vault Boy is based off the *Fallout: New Vegas* perk Jury Rigging. The *Fallout: The Roleplaying Game* version of Jury Rigging also uses the Licensed Plumber version of the Vault Boy.

Other perks that increase durability include:

- Gunsmith - ranged weapons
- Makeshift Warrior - melee weapons
- Power Patcher - power armor
- Stable Tools - power tools
- White Knight - armor
